q: How many people accompanied Ibrahim (alayhis salam) during the Hijra from Mesopotamia to Palestine?
exp: Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was accompanied by his wife Sarah and his nephew Lut (peace be upon him).

q: From the hadith: “The inhabitants of Paradise will have a comb made of gold, and the incense burner will contain...” What will be in the incense burner?
exp: In the hadith in al-Bukhari about the people of Paradise, their censers will burn oud (aloeswood) and their combs will be of gold.

q: Which month is the best, and which month has the best day?
exp: The best month is Ramadan, and the best day of the year — the Day of Arafah (or the Day of Sacrifice) — falls in Dhul-Hijjah.

q: From the hadith: Jibril (alayhis salam) commanded the Prophet ﷺ to pray in the valley, which is sacred to Allah. What is it called?
What is tawassul in Islam?
a: Ways of drawing closer to Allah
Reliance on Allah in all matters
Turning to Allah without using means
Abandoning causes for the sake of reliance
exp: Tawassul means seeking nearness to Allah through permitted means: His names and attributes, one's own righteous deeds, or the supplication of a living righteous person.

q: From the hadith: "Buthan is one of the rivers of Paradise." Where is the valley of Buthan on earth?
exp: Buthan is a valley in Medina; a hadith says it lies on one of the channels of Paradise.

q: According to the majority of scholars, is the basmallah an ayah of Surah Al-Fatiha?
a: It is part of all surahs of the Qur'an
exp: According to the Hanafis, Malikis and most Hanbalis, the basmala is not a verse of Al-Fatiha; the Shafi'is consider it a verse.

q: Which surah in the Qur'an does not begin with the basmallah?
exp: Surah At-Tawbah is the only surah of the Quran that does not begin with the basmala.

q: In which year of the Hijri was fasting prescribed?
exp: Fasting in Ramadan was prescribed in the 2nd year of the Hijra, after the migration to Medina.

q: Itikaf is seclusion for worship in a mosque. Where is it performed (minimum condition)?
a: Only in a mosque where Juma prayer is held
In any designated place for prayer
exp: I'tikaf is performed in a mosque. Malikis and Shafi'is allow any mosque; Hanafis and Hanbalis require a mosque where congregational prayers are held.

q: Complete the hadith: “The smell coming from the mouth of a fasting person is better with Allah than the aroma of...”?
exp: The hadith says: “The smell from the mouth of a fasting person is better to Allah than the fragrance of musk” (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: Which of the following was the scribe of the Prophet ﷺ?
exp: Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan (may Allah be pleased with him) was one of the Prophet's ﷺ scribes, writing down revelation and letters.

q: What is al-mu'awwidhatayn?
a: The last three suras of the Qur'an
The last two suras of the Qur'an (Al-Falak and An-Nas)
exp: Al-Mu'awwidhatayn are the two protective surahs, Al-Falaq and An-Nas; both begin with “Say: I seek refuge…”.

q: Which of the scribes of the Prophet ﷺ did Abu Bakr al-Siddiq commission to collect the Koran?
exp: Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) entrusted Zayd ibn Thabit — a leading scribe of the revelation who witnessed the final review of the Quran with Jibril — with compiling it.

q: What is remarkable about the last two verses of Surah At-Tauba (Laqad Jaakum) when they were written down during the compilation of the Qur'an?
a: Their written record was found only with Abu Khuzayma al-Ansari
They were copied from Hafsa's scrolls
They were transmitted only by Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman
They were added during the reign of Uthman
exp: Zayd ibn Thabit reported that he found the written record of the last verses of At-Tawbah only with Abu Khuzaymah al-Ansari, although many knew them by heart (al-Bukhari).

q: Which of these names of Allah in the Qur'an is used only for Allah and not for creation?
exp: The name Ar-Rahman is used only for Allah, whereas a created being may be described as merciful, hearing or peaceful.

q: Allah has a hundred mercies. How many of them did He leave on earth, and how many did He keep with Himself until the Day of Judgment?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said Allah has one hundred mercies: He sent down one to His creation and kept ninety-nine for the Day of Judgement (Muslim).

q: Complete the hadith: “Each ummah had its own characteristic feature. A characteristic feature of my ummah is...”
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Every religion has a distinctive trait, and the trait of Islam is modesty (haya)” (Ibn Majah).

q: What is an article of faith?
exp: Aqidah is the creed: what a Muslim firmly believes in his heart.

q: What is the name in Islam for the time equal to half the interval from Maghrib (sunset) to Fajr (true dawn)?
a: Beginning of the first third of the night
exp: The Islamic midnight is the midpoint between sunset (Maghrib) and true dawn (Fajr); the preferred time of Isha lasts until then.

q: What is a religious-legal school in Islam?
exp: A madhhab is a school of law, a method of deriving Islamic rulings; the best known are the Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i and Hanbali schools.

q: Which sura begins with the last part of the Quran, revealed only to the Prophet ﷺ?
exp: The last part of the Quran, al-Mufassal, according to the best-known view begins with Surah Qaf; the Prophet ﷺ said it was given to him in addition to what earlier prophets received.

q: A person who breaks an oath must feed 10 poor people. What is this atonement called?
exp: Kaffarah is the expiation for a broken oath: feeding or clothing ten poor people or freeing a slave, and if that is impossible, fasting three days (5:89).

q: Fleeing from the battlefield is...
exp: Fleeing from the battlefield is listed in the hadith among the seven destructive sins (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: What is the entrance to prayer and the exit from it?
exp: The hadith says: “The key to prayer is purification, it is entered by takbir and exited by taslim” (Abu Dawud, at-Tirmidhi).

q: Jalsat al-istiraha is a short sitting after sajda while standing up. If a person, out of forgetfulness, sat in this position longer than usual, what should he do?
a: Makes two prostrations of forgetfulness (sujud as-sahw)
Does nothing and ends the prayer as usual
There is no such posture in prayer
exp: If one forgetfully prolongs a sitting that should be brief, one makes sujud as-sahw — two prostrations of forgetfulness — at the end of the prayer.

q: How many places of prostration of recitation (sujud at-tilawah) are mentioned in the hadith of Amr ibn al-As?
exp: The hadith of Amr ibn al-As mentions 15 places of prostration of recitation in the Quran; some scholars count 14, and the Malikis 11.

q: According to the Hanafi madhhab, what is the legal status of congregational prayer for men?
exp: In the Hanafi school, congregational prayer is wajib for men (another view in the school: an emphasised sunnah close to wajib).

q: What is the minimum number of people required to perform congregational prayer?
a: 1 person, as angels and jinn from among Muslims stand behind him
exp: A congregational prayer can be held with just two people: an imam and one person praying with him.

q: A person wants to go to collective prayer in a mosque, but his creditor is there and he cannot repay his debt. Is this considered a valid reason not to go to the mosque?
a: No, because all the mosques might be empty in this case
Yes, this is a valid reason
exp: Scholars count an insolvent debtor's fear of a creditor who may detain him among valid excuses for missing congregational prayer.

q: A Muslim recognizes the obligation of zakat, but does not pay it out of greed. What is its status in Islam?
a: He will still be considered a Muslim
He will be considered an apostate
exp: Whoever acknowledges that zakat is obligatory but withholds it out of stinginess commits a major sin but does not leave Islam; denying its obligation is disbelief.

q: Complete the hadith: “The best food is that food...”.
a: Which is good for the body
Which is earned with your own hands
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “No one has eaten better food than what he earned with his own hands” (al-Bukhari).

q: Which obligatory prayer is the fourth in time during the day?
exp: Counting from dawn, the order is Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha, so Maghrib is the fourth.

q: Which name of Makkah is mentioned in the Qur'an (3:96)?
exp: “Indeed, the first House established for mankind is the one at Bakkah” (3:96); Bakkah is one of the names of Mecca.

q: In the book “Sharh al-Sira”, Ibn Abdul-Barr claims that the migration of the Prophet ﷺ to Medina after the ascension occurred through...?
exp: According to the view cited by Ibn Abd al-Barr, the Hijra took place one year and two months after the Ascension (Mi'raj); other opinions exist.

q: How many verses are there in the Qur'an about Allah's ascension to the Throne?
exp: Allah's rising over the Throne (istiwa) is mentioned in seven places in the Quran, e.g. 7:54 and 20:5.

q: Surah Al-Baqarah, verses 58–59: Allah ordered to say “hitta” (forgive us), and they said “hinta” (wheat), for which they were punished. Who are they?
exp: This refers to the Children of Israel: instead of saying “hittah” (forgive us), they distorted the word and were punished (2:58–59).

q: 10th century, Cordoba, Andalusia: which madhhab was practiced in Spain?
exp: The Maliki school prevailed in al-Andalus, including Córdoba.

q: Sura 3:37: Every time Zakaria (alayhis salaam) entered her prayer room, he found food from her. To the question “Oh Maryam! Where did you get this from? she replied: “This is from Allah.” What is the name of this miracle?
exp: A karamah is a wonder Allah grants to a righteous person who is not a prophet; a mu'jizah is a prophet's miracle. Maryam was not a prophet, so this is a karamah.

q: Which tribe from Yemen stopped at the spring of Zamzam with the permission of the Hajars?
exp: With Hajar's permission, the Yemeni tribe of Jurhum settled by Zamzam; Isma'il (peace be upon him) grew up among them (al-Bukhari).

q: In the pre-Islamic era, what idol did the Arabs have on the shores of the Red Sea?
exp: The idol Manat stood near the Red Sea coast at al-Mushallal near Qudayd, between Mecca and Medina.

q: The sun had long since deviated from its zenith, and the shadow of the object had almost reached its length. What is the prayer time?
exp: Dhuhr lasts until an object's shadow equals its length (excluding the midday shadow); if the shadow has only almost reached the object's length, it is still Dhuhr.

q: The imam performed namaz, placing one person on his left and another on his right. Will such prayer be permissible?
a: There will be a condition if they are women
exp: Such a prayer is valid — Ibn Mas'ud prayed with two people on either side — but the Sunnah is for two followers to stand behind the imam.

q: What is a dog?
exp: Sabaq is a prize in contests such as racing or archery; the hadith says: “No prize except in camel racing, horse racing and archery.”

q: What is Hiba?
exp: Hibah is transferring property to another free of charge, i.e. a gift.

q: In the hadiths about hijama (cupping), preferred days of the month are mentioned. Which?
exp: A hadith names the 17th, 19th and 21st of the lunar month as preferred days for hijamah (Abu Dawud).

q: According to the hadith of al-Bukhari, Allah accelerates the punishment in this world for two: the oppressor and the one who...
exp: The hadith says: “Two sins Allah punishes already in this world: oppression and disrespect to parents” (al-Bukhari, al-Adab al-Mufrad).

q: From the hadith: whoever washes his head and body on the day of Juma, goes out early, catches the sermon, walks and not on horseback, and listens to the imam without being distracted - he will receive a reward for every step...
a: Forgiveness of one sin and elevation by one step
For fasting and praying for a whole year
Forgiveness of sins for the past and next week
exp: According to the hadith of Aws ibn Aws, each step such a person takes to Jumu'ah earns the reward of a year of fasting and prayer (Abu Dawud, at-Tirmidhi).

q: Whoever learns the first 10 verses of this surah will be protected from the turmoil of the Dajjal. What sura are we talking about?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever memorises the first ten verses of Surah Al-Kahf will be protected from the Dajjal” (Muslim).

q: According to the hadith, whoever recites this surah on Fridays will be endowed with light on the Day of Judgment. What sura are we talking about?
exp: Reading Surah Al-Kahf on Friday brings light — between two Fridays, and in some narrations on the Day of Judgement.

q: According to the hadith, this world is given for temporary use, and the best of it is...
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “This world is an enjoyment, and the best of its enjoyment is a righteous wife” (Muslim).

q: From the hadith: whoever in a day combines four deeds — visits the sick, attends a funeral, fasts and ... — will be written among the people of Paradise. What is the fourth deed?
exp: In the hadith in Muslim, the four deeds are fasting, attending a funeral, visiting the sick and feeding a poor person (charity) — whoever combines them in a day will enter Paradise.

q: From the hadith: In the place of Al-Muhammas, the Prophet ﷺ performed this prayer with the ascetics and said that it was offered to those who came before you, but they neglected it, and you are given a double reward for treating it with care. What kind of prayer is this?
exp: The hadith in Muslim refers to Asr: this prayer was offered to earlier nations, but they neglected it.

q: From Aisha (radiyallahu anha): If Allah desires good for a house, then He bestows on its inhabitants...
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “When Allah wants good for the people of a household, He brings gentleness into it” (Ahmad).

q: According to the hadith, the inhabitants of Paradise will fill 120 rows. How many of them will be Muslims?
exp: The hadith in at-Tirmidhi says the people of Paradise will form 120 rows, 80 of them from the ummah of Muhammad ﷺ.

q: From the hadith: Friday prayer is obligatory for everyone except four: women, children, the sick and.... Who's fourth?
exp: Jumu'ah is obligatory on every Muslim except four: a slave, a woman, a child and a sick person (Abu Dawud).

q: From the hadith: The width of my reservoir will be from the place where I stand to .... Complete the hadith.
exp: The Prophet ﷺ described the width of his Pool (al-Hawd) as the distance to Amman in al-Sham (at-Tirmidhi).

q: According to the hadith, what is jihad of the old man, the child, the weak and the woman?
a: Providing ammunition for those going to jihad
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The jihad of the elderly, the young, the weak and women is Hajj and Umrah” (an-Nasa'i).

q: From the hadith: On the Day of Judgment, when the scholars are brought to the Throne of Allah, ... will confidently walk ahead of them. Who is this?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said that on the Day of Judgement Mu'adh ibn Jabal will come ahead of the scholars by a stone's throw; he was among the most knowledgeable Companions in what is lawful and unlawful.

q: Raising hands in prayer with takbir: after ruku'a, before sazhda and when standing up after tashahhud. What's the reward?
a: Elevation by one degree in Paradise
exp: A report from Uqbah ibn Amir states that each raising of the hands in prayer earns ten good deeds.

q: When standing up after the first tashahhud, takbir and raising of hands are performed...
exp: When rising after the first tashahhud, the takbir is said during the movement of getting up.

q: Is it permissible to raise hands between two sujuds?
a: No, it is not allowed (not established in the Sunnah)
exp: Ibn Umar reported that the Prophet ﷺ raised his hands at the opening takbir, bowing and rising from it, but did not do so between the prostrations (al-Bukhari).

q: The Koran is divided into Juz, Hizb and Rub'a. How many rub'a are in the Koran? Rub'a are marked with an asterisk at the beginning of the verse.
exp: The Quran has 30 juz', each of 2 hizbs, each of 4 rub'; in total 30 × 2 × 4 = 240 rub'.

q: Voluntary prayer (nafl), performed where people cannot see it, is superior to prayer in front of people...
exp: A hadith says a voluntary prayer offered where people do not see it surpasses one offered in front of them twenty-five times.

q: From the hadith: A hypocrite will not combine two qualities - commendable religiosity and...
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Two qualities are never combined in a hypocrite: good conduct and understanding of the religion (fiqh)” (at-Tirmidhi).

q: Complete the hadith: “Everyone who is rude, ..., proud will end up in Hell.”
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Shall I tell you about the people of Hell? Every harsh, greedy (hoarding) and arrogant person” (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: What is it called when a jurist prefers a stronger proof over direct analogy (qiyas) in reaching a ruling?
exp: Istihsan is preferring a stronger proof over direct analogy (qiyas); its critics accused it of relying on personal preference.

q: According to the Hanbali madhhab, is continuity (muwalat) a required condition for wudu?
exp: For the Hanbalis, continuity (muwalat) in wudu is obligatory: one must not pause so long that the previously washed limb dries.

q: Rububiyya, Uluhiyya and Asma wa-Sifat are parts of...
exp: Tawhid is divided into three categories: lordship (rububiyyah), worship (uluhiyyah), and names and attributes (asma wa sifat).

q: What is Sujud al-Sahw?
a: Two prostrations performed due to forgetfulness in prayer (before or after salam)
Prostration performed when reciting certain verses of the Qur'an
Prostration of gratitude to Allah for good news
exp: Sujud as-sahw is two prostrations that make up for an omission or mistake made forgetfully in prayer.

q: How many variants of large salavat are known?
exp: Several wordings of the Ibrahimi salawat are reported in authentic hadiths — seven by the count of some scholars.

q: Which of the two expressions is correct in salawat according to the Sunnah?
a: Both expressions refer to the Sunnah
Expressions are equivalent, but preferable without the words “our master”
exp: The Prophet ﷺ taught the Companions the salawat without the words “our master”: “Allahumma salli ‘ala Muhammad…” (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: Do the following words belong to the established form of salawat: "to Muhammad son of Abdullah", "Seal of the Prophets", "Imam of the God-fearing", "Messenger of Mercy"?
a: Yes, all of the above expressions are sunnah
Only the words "Seal of the Prophets" are sunnah
Only "to Muhammad son of Abdullah" is sunnah
These expressions are allowed but are not the established form of salawat
exp: These epithets are true in meaning, but they are not in the wordings of salawat transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ, so in prayer one keeps to the transmitted text.

q: According to the Hanafi madhhab, the dua qunut in witr prayer is read...
exp: In the Hanafi school, qunut is recited in the third rak'ah of witr throughout the year, not only in Ramadan.

q: According to the Hanafi madhhab, in witr prayer the dua qunut is read...
a: At the discretion of the imam
exp: Hanafis recite qunut in witr before bowing: after the recitation they say takbir raising the hands, then make the supplication.

q: A hadith in which one or more narrators are missing at the beginning of the isnad is called...
exp: A mu'allaq hadith is one where one or more narrators are omitted at the beginning of the chain (on the compiler's side).

q: When these words are spoken in the morning, Allah protects you until the evening, and in the evening until the morning from Satan. What is this?
exp: For example, about Ayat al-Kursi it is reported: whoever recites it in the morning is protected from Shaytan until evening, and in the evening — until morning (an-Nasa'i, al-Hakim).

q: The man performed the Isha prayer closer to midnight, and after the third part of the night came, he performed 11 rak'ahs. What kind of ‘ibadat is this?
exp: Qiyam al-layl is any night prayer after Isha; tahajjud is night prayer after sleeping. No sleep is mentioned here, so the answer is qiyam al-layl.

q: Which of the obligatory prayers is better to perform closer to the end of its time?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said he would delay Isha to a third or half of the night were it not hard on his community (at-Tirmidhi).

q: Which prayer is better to perform immediately when its time comes?
exp: Maghrib has a short time window, and the Prophet ﷺ prayed it right after sunset.

q: A verse was revealed about those who were killed at the well of Ma'un. What sura is it in?
a: There is no such verse in the Koran
exp: A verse was revealed about those killed at Bi'r Ma'unah, but its recitation was later abrogated, so it is not in the Mushaf (al-Bukhari).

q: How was the prohibition of wine established in the Qur'an?
a: Gradually in three stages (Al-Baqarah 2:219, An-Nisa 4:43, Al-Maida 5:90-91)
There is no prohibition in the Qur'an
exp: Wine was prohibited gradually: first its harm was said to outweigh its benefit (2:219), then praying while intoxicated was forbidden (4:43), then it was banned completely (5:90–91).

q: A person in ihram performs Hajj wearing ordinary (stitched) clothes. Is his Hajj valid?
a: Valid, but he must offer expiation (fidyah)
Valid, but greatly reduced in reward
exp: Wearing ordinary (stitched) clothing while in ihram is a violation requiring expiation (fidyah), but the Hajj remains valid.

q: In what century did a separate science of interpretation of the Koran emerge, the founders of which were at-Tabari and Ibn Abu Hatim?
exp: Tafsir took shape as a distinct science by the end of the 3rd century AH, i.e. the early 10th century CE: at-Tabari died in 310 AH (923 CE), Ibn Abi Hatim in 327 AH.

q: Al-Bukhari (from Umm Shariq, radilahu anha): The Prophet ﷺ ordered the killing of lizards because they fanned the fire of Ibrahim (alayhis salaam). What kind of lizard are we talking about?
exp: This is the gecko (al-wazagh): the hadith says it blew on the fire into which Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was thrown (al-Bukhari).

q: Al-As ibn Wail ground the bone into powder and said to the Prophet ﷺ: “Will Allah really revive this after death?” And then the last verses of the sura were revealed...
exp: The verses were revealed: “Who will give life to bones that have rotted? Say: He who created them the first time will give them life” (36:78–79).

q: According to the Cairo edition of the Koran, how many Meccan and Madinan suras are there?
exp: In the 1924 Cairo edition of the Quran, 86 surahs are marked Meccan and 28 Medinan.

q: “For those who believed and did righteous deeds, there is no sin for what they ate...” - who does this verse refer to? (Al-Maida, 5:93)
a: The verse has a general meaning and applies to everyone
About Companions who died before wine was prohibited
exp: When wine was prohibited, people asked about Companions who had drunk it before the ban and died (some fell at Uhud); then this verse was revealed (al-Bukhari).

q: How many days, according to the Qur'an, did the creation of the heavens and the earth take?
exp: Allah created the heavens and the earth in six days (7:54, 10:3 and other verses).

q: “Today, for your sake, I have perfected your religion, completed My mercy upon you, and approved Islam as a religion for you.” Indicate the surah and verse.
exp: This is verse 5:3 of Al-Ma'idah, revealed on the Day of Arafah during the Farewell Hajj.

q: Ibn Abbas (radiyallahu anhu) reported: when the Prophet ﷺ arrived in Medina, its inhabitants deceived each other to the extent. Then Allah sent down the sura... and they began to measure honestly.
exp: Surah Al-Mutaffifin (“Those who give short measure”) opens with: “Woe to those who give short measure!” (83:1).

q: The name of Allah "Al-Mubin" means...
a: The Manifest, the One who makes clear
exp: Al-Mubin is the Manifest, the One who makes clear: Allah's truth is evident, and He makes the path of truth clear to His servants.

q: In the hadith about the Sirat it is said that this is the place where...
exp: The hadith describes the Sirat as a slippery place where feet cannot stand firm (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: Which of the following is included in the menu of the inhabitants of Hell?
exp: The Quran mentions zaqqum (44:43–44), thorny dari' (88:6) and pus ghislin (69:36) as food of the people of Hell.

q: Reading the Koran in prayer silently, but a little louder than a whisper, is called...
exp: Dandanah is a low murmur whose words others cannot make out; the term was used for quiet recitation and supplication.

q: The name of Allah "Al-Latif" means...
exp: Al-Latif is the Subtle, who knows the finest details, and the Kind, who bestows grace in imperceptible ways.

q: What is miqat?
a: The set boundaries that cannot be crossed without ihram (for Hajj and 'Umrah)
exp: A miqat is a fixed boundary that a pilgrim heading for Hajj or Umrah must not cross without entering ihram.

q: You are flying from Europe to Mecca. What is the name of the place of entry into ihram for Hajj and Umrah?
exp: Al-Juhfah is the miqat for those coming from al-Sham, Egypt and the Maghrib; most flights from Europe pass it, and today ihram is entered at Rabigh or when crossing its line.

q: What is the name of the miqat for those traveling from Medina to Mecca?
exp: Dhul-Hulayfah (Abyar Ali) is the miqat for the people of Medina and those travelling through it; it is the farthest miqat from Mecca.

q: How many mikats are there in total?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ set five miqats: Dhul-Hulayfah, al-Juhfah, Qarn al-Manazil, Yalamlam and Dhat Irq.

q: If a person passes the miqat without ihram and does not return to it, will his pilgrimage be valid?
a: Yes, but he must offer expiation (dam)
Only if he returns to the miqat and enters ihram again
exp: Whoever passes the miqat without ihram and does not return still has a valid pilgrimage but must offer a sacrificial animal (dam).

q: From the hadith: “Truly, whoever is endowed with ... has been given a great portion of this world and the next; support of family ties, good morals and good attitude towards neighbors revitalize villages and add life span.” What are we talking about?
exp: In the hadith from Aishah: “Whoever is given gentleness has been given a great share of the good of this world and the next” (Ahmad).

q: From a hadith from Anas ibn Malik (radiyallahu anhu): The Prophet ﷺ said: “Take qaylulu (a short nap), truly...”
a: The devils do not rest during the day
Jews do not like to sleep during the day
exp: The hadith says: “Take a midday nap (qaylulah), for the devils do not nap” (at-Tabarani).

q: From the hadith: “There is no problem in wealth for a God-fearing person, and health for a God-fearing person is better than wealth, and ... is one of the pleasures of this world.”
exp: The hadith says: “…and cheerfulness of heart is one of the blessings of this world” (Ibn Majah).

q: From the hadith: “Wet your family ties, at least...”
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Keep ties of kinship, even if only with a greeting of salam” (al-Bazzar).

q: From the hadith: “Verily, on the Day of Judgment Allah will cry: Where are My neighbors?” Who are they?
a: Loved each other for the sake of Allah
Those who filled the mosques with worship
exp: The hadith says Allah will call those who filled the mosques with worship His neighbours.

q: From a hadith from Abu Said and Abu Hurairah (radiyallahu anhum): “Rulers will come to you who will bring the worst people closer and will delay prayer.” What should a Muslim do?
a: Not to be a collector of zakat and a custodian of property
exp: In the hadith, the Prophet ﷺ instructs not to serve such rulers as an overseer, guard, tax collector or treasurer (Ibn Hibban).

q: It is narrated from Abu Hurairah (radiyallahu anhu) that the Prophet ﷺ said: “If someone ruled at least ten people, then on the Day of Judgment he will be brought bound, and only untie him... otherwise his oppression will destroy him.” Sahih Muslim (No. 2621). What ends the hadith?
exp: The hadith says: “…and nothing will free him except his justice, or else his injustice will destroy him.”

q: “The angels will be on its edge, and ... will carry over them the Throne of your Lord” (Surah Al-Haqqa, 69:17). How many are there?
exp: “…and eight (angels) will bear the Throne of your Lord above them that Day” (69:17).

q: Whoever washes the deceased and hides what he saw on him, Allah will forgive him... once.
exp: The hadith says: “Whoever washes a deceased person and conceals what he sees, Allah forgives him forty times” (al-Hakim).

q: Is it permissible for a woman to bathe a deceased man and vice versa?
a: It is permissible if the husband washes his wife and the wife of her husband
Allowed only in the absence of relatives of the same sex
exp: Spouses may wash each other: Ali washed Fatimah, and Asma bint Umays washed Abu Bakr. The Hanafis permit it only for the wife.

q: If the child died in the womb before 4 months, then...
exp: A foetus miscarried before four months, before the soul is breathed into it, is not washed, shrouded or prayed over; it is wrapped in cloth and buried.

q: How many grams of silver were equal to dirhams at the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?
exp: The Islamic dirham weighed about 2.975 g of silver, roughly 3 g; the zakat nisab is 200 dirhams ≈ 595 g of silver.

q: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Power: its beginning is reproach, its middle is regret, and its end is ... except the one who showed justice.”
a: Punishment on the Day of Judgment
exp: The Prophet ﷺ warned that authority begins with blame, continues with regret and ends in punishment on the Day of Judgement unless one was just (at-Tabarani).

q: The rewards for the martyr are great. Which of the following **not** applies to this hadith?
a: With the first drop of blood spilled, all his sins are forgiven.
He will be shown his place in Paradise
He will be clothed in the robe of faith
He will sit on a bench made of nur
exp: The hadith on the martyr's rewards does not mention a bench of light; it mentions forgiveness with the first drop of blood, being shown his place in Paradise, protection from the punishment of the grave and being clothed in the garment of faith (at-Tirmidhi, Ahmad).

q: On the night of the Ascension the Prophet ﷺ saw written on the gate of Paradise: “Charity is rewarded tenfold, and an interest-free loan — ...”
exp: The hadith says: “…charity is rewarded tenfold and an interest-free loan eighteenfold”, because only a person in need asks for a loan (Ibn Majah).

q: “The first thing you will lose from your religion will be amana (trust), and the last thing will be...”
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The first thing you will lose of your religion is trust (amanah), and the last is prayer” (at-Tabarani).

q: According to the Sunnah, when entering a mosque, which foot should be placed first?
a: Right foot when entering and left foot when exiting
Right foot on entry and right foot on exit
Left foot on entry and right foot on exit
It makes no difference as long as you go to the mosque
exp: According to the Sunnah, one enters the mosque with the right foot and leaves with the left; the right is preferred for honourable things.

q: From ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan (radiyallahu anhu): The Prophet ﷺ said that Allah brought into Paradise a person who was easy in buying and selling, and also...
a: Shortened and combined prayers on the way
He gave alms so that his left hand did not know what his right hand was doing.
When repaying and when demanding repayment of a debt
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Allah admitted to Paradise a man who was lenient when buying, selling, repaying and demanding repayment” (Ahmad, an-Nasa'i).

q: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The prayer of two does not rise above the head: the slave who ran away from his master until he returns, and...”
a: A woman who disobeys her husband, until she stops
A person harassing a neighbor until he stops
A person who spreads gossip until he stops
A guardian who improperly spends the orphan's property
exp: The hadith says the prayers of a runaway slave and of a wife who disobeys her husband do not rise above their heads until they return to what is right (al-Hakim, at-Tabarani).

q: The testimony of which companion did the Prophet ﷺ equate to the testimony of two men?
exp: Khuzaymah ibn Thabit testified for the Prophet ﷺ in a dispute with a Bedouin out of belief in him, and the Prophet ﷺ made his testimony equal to that of two men (Abu Dawud).

q: In what century according to the Hijri did Abu al-Aswad al-Duali first begin to place vowels in the Koran?
exp: Abu al-Aswad ad-Du'ali (d. 69 AH) was the first to mark vowels in the Quran with dots, in the 1st century AH.

q: One of the first editions of the Quran printed in Arabic movable type appeared in 1694. In which city?
exp: In 1694 in Hamburg, Abraham Hinckelmann printed the Arabic text of the Quran with movable type.

q: What surah did the Prophet ﷺ read in prayer before his departure from this world?
a: The last verses of Surah Al-Hashr
exp: Umm al-Fadl heard the Prophet ﷺ recite Al-Mursalat in Maghrib, and he did not lead them in prayer after that until he passed away (al-Bukhari).

q: Where did the Prophet ﷺ change the qibla during prayer after the revelation of the verse (Al-Baqarah 2:144)?
a: In Medina (Masjid Banu Salama, Masjid al-Qiblatayn)
exp: The qiblah was changed in Medina; the mosque of Banu Salimah, where worshippers turned during the prayer, became known as Masjid al-Qiblatayn (“mosque of the two qiblahs”).

q: How long after the Hijra was the verse about the change of the qibla revealed?
exp: For 16–17 months after the Hijra Muslims prayed towards Jerusalem, then the qiblah was turned to the Ka'bah (al-Bukhari).

q: Before the Hijra, during bowing from the waist, Muslims crossed their hands and placed them between their knees. Who prayed like that?
exp: This hand position (tatbiq) was practised in early Islam and later abrogated with the command to place the palms on the knees (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: What is the position of the heels during Sujud?
exp: Scholars differ: according to the hadith of Aishah the heels are joined in prostration, while other views keep them apart; both are acceptable.

q: What is the name of the shaitan who distracts you during prayer?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said the devil who distracts one in prayer is called Khinzab and instructed seeking refuge in Allah from him (Muslim).

q: What should be said when passing by a cemetery of non-believers?
a: There is no prescribed greeting; it is better to remain silent
We give them tidings of the Fire
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Wherever you pass by the grave of a disbeliever, give him tidings of the Fire” (Ibn Majah, 1573; graded authentic by al-Albani).

q: Who hears the punishment in the grave?
a: All creatures except humans and jinn
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said the cry of one punished in the grave is heard by all creatures except humans and jinn (al-Bukhari).

q: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Do not laugh excessively, for excessive laughter…”. What is he doing?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Do not laugh much, for much laughter deadens the heart” (Ibn Majah).

q: The inhabitants of Paradise will enter there without body hair, without beard, with eyes tinted with antimony, at the age of... years?
exp: The hadith says the people of Paradise will enter it hairless, beardless, with kohl-lined eyes, aged 33 (at-Tirmidhi).

q: The Prophet ﷺ blessed some dates in a small bag and gave it to Abu Hurayrah, who ate from it for years. When was the bag lost?
a: On the day Uthman was killed
On the day of the Battle of Siffin
exp: Abu Hurayrah said he ate from this bag during the time of the Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman, and it was lost on the day Uthman was killed (at-Tirmidhi).

q: Which is the Sunnah when entering a house?
exp: When entering a home, one mentions Allah (Bismillah) and greets its people with salam: “When you enter houses, greet one another” (24:61).

q: Where was Caliph ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan (radiyAllahu anhu) born?
exp: According to a common view among historians, Uthman ibn Affan was born in Ta'if about six years after the Year of the Elephant.

q: What opens the “door” to prayer?
exp: Prayer begins with the opening takbir (“Allahu akbar”), after which everything outside the prayer becomes forbidden.

q: Where do the “middle” suras of the mufassal begin and end?
exp: According to one view, the “middle” mufassal runs from Surah Al-Buruj to Surah Al-Bayyinah; other divisions exist.

q: Which two suras are called "Tulayain"?
exp: “At-Tulayayn” (the two long ones) are Al-An'am and Al-A'raf; the Prophet ﷺ recited the longer of them in Maghrib.

q: Who are the people on the heights (Al-A'raf) according to the most common interpretation?
a: Those whose good deeds equal their sins
Those who went to jihad without parental permission
exp: In the common interpretation, the people of al-A'raf are those whose good and bad deeds are equal; ultimately they will enter Paradise by Allah's mercy.

q: How will the wine of the inhabitants of Paradise be sealed? (Al-Muttaffifin, 26)
exp: “They will be given a sealed pure drink, whose seal is musk” (83:25–26).

q: How many sons did the prophet Ismail (alaihassalam) have?
exp: Historians and the Torah mention twelve sons of Isma'il (peace be upon him), from whom Arab tribes, including Quraysh, descend.

q: How many years did the secret call of the Prophet ﷺ last in Mecca?
exp: For the first three years the Prophet ﷺ called to Islam secretly, until the verse “Proclaim openly what you are commanded” was revealed (15:94).

q: How many years did the open call of the Prophet ﷺ last in Mecca?
exp: The open call in Mecca lasted about ten years, until the Hijra; the whole Meccan period was 13 years.

q: Who was the first of the children to accept Islam?
exp: The first child to accept Islam was Ali ibn Abi Talib, who grew up in the Prophet's ﷺ house; the first woman was Khadijah, the first free man Abu Bakr, the first freed slave Zayd.

q: How to understand the words: “Glorify your Lord in the evening and in the morning” (Ghafir, 55)?
a: Read askars in the evening and in the morning
Say tasbih, tahmid, tahlil and takbir
exp: Many exegetes understand this glorification as prayer — in the evening and morning (Asr and Fajr).

q: Who said about the Prophet ﷺ: “This is nothing but transmitted witchcraft,” and mentioned in Al-Muddassir 74:11–26?
exp: Verses 74:11–26 were revealed about al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, who acknowledged the power of the Quran but, to please his tribe, called it “magic handed down”.

q: What is the position of the hands when raised during takbir in prayer?
a: All options are related to the sunnah
exp: All three are reported in hadiths — raising the hands before, together with, and after the takbir — so all are Sunnah.

q: What is the minimum threshold (nisab) for theft at which the thief's hand is cut off?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The hand is cut for a quarter of a dinar or more” (al-Bukhari, Muslim); the Hanafis set the threshold at ten dirhams.

q: What should be done with a lost item whose owner is not found?
a: Search for owner 1 year, then you may use it while remaining obliged to return
exp: The Prophet ﷺ ordered announcing a found item for a year; if the owner does not appear it may be used, but must be returned if he comes later (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: These two rivers have their source from Paradise. Which?
exp: In the hadiths of the Ascension, the Prophet ﷺ saw two outer rivers at the Lote Tree — the Nile and the Euphrates (al-Bukhari); Muslim lists them among the rivers of Paradise.

q: What was the origin of Prophet Ibrahim (alaihassalam)?
exp: Ibrahim (peace be upon him) came from Mesopotamia, the land of the Chaldeans (the city of Ur), from where he migrated to al-Sham.

q: “Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve, in the Book of Allah on the day He created the heavens and the earth.” In which surah is this verse?
exp: The verse about twelve months, four of them sacred, is 9:36 of Surah At-Tawbah.

q: Which scholar pointed to the Earth's roundness based on the words “He wraps the night over the day” (39:5)?
exp: Ibn Hazm cited this verse in al-Fisal: the verb yukawwiru — to wind, like a turban — points to the Earth's roundness.

q: About whom it was said: “Ask! I swear by Allah, no matter what question you ask me, I will give an answer about any verse: whether it was revealed at night or during the day, on the plain or in the mountains. He knows both the obvious and the hidden from the Qur'an"?
exp: Ali ibn Abi Talib said these words about himself, urging people to ask him about the Quran, since he knew where and when each verse was revealed.

q: Name the longest verse in the Qur'an.
exp: The longest verse of the Quran is the verse of debt, 2:282 of Surah Al-Baqarah.

q: To whom was the Zabur revealed?
exp: “…and to Dawud We gave the Zabur” (4:163).

q: What will come on the Day of Judgment with two eyes and a tongue and testify?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said Allah will raise the Black Stone on the Day of Judgement with two eyes to see and a tongue to testify for those who touched it sincerely (at-Tirmidhi).

q: Who can see an angel?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “When you hear a rooster crow, ask Allah of His bounty, for it has seen an angel” (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: Where and when was the verse from Surah Al-Maida, 5:3, revealed: “Today I have perfected your religion for your sake...”?
a: In Haram Mecca on the day of the capture of Mecca by Muslims
On Friday, on Mount Arafat, during the Farewell Hajj
In Medina, on Friday, two days before the death of the Prophet ﷺ
exp: Umar confirmed that verse 5:3 was revealed on a Friday, the Day of Arafah, during the Farewell Hajj (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: Surah Al-Maida, verse 67: “...and Allah will protect you from...” From whom?
exp: “O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you… Allah will protect you from the people” (5:67); after this verse the Prophet ﷺ dismissed his guards.

q: In Surah Al-Qasas, 28:24, Musa (alaihassalam) said: “Lord! Verily, I need every good thing that You bestow upon me.” What events preceded this?
a: When Musa (alayhassalam) killed an Egyptian and was afraid
When he helped the two daughters of Shu'ayb (alayhassalam) by moving a stone from the well
When Pharaoh gathered sorcerers to compete with Musa (alaihassalam)
When Musa (alayhassalam) stood by the Red Sea and saw the army of Pharaoh
exp: In Madyan, Musa (peace be upon him) watered the flocks of two young women, daughters of a righteous old man, then withdrew to the shade and made this supplication (28:23–24).

q: What supplication did Musa (peace be upon him) make in Madyan after watering the flocks of two young women?
a: “My Lord, I am in need of whatever good You send down to me”
“My Lord, expand my chest for me”
“There is no god but You, glory be to You”
exp: “So he watered their flocks, then turned to the shade and said: ‘My Lord, I am in need of whatever good You send down to me’” (28:24).

q: The hadith says: “During Sujud, do not be like a dog.” What do you mean?
a: Don't put your elbows on the ground
Don't wag your body like a dog's tail
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Be balanced in prostration and do not spread your forearms like a dog” (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: From the hadith: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was granted 6 advantages over the prophets. Which of the following **isn't** included in these six?
a: The words given to me are laconic, but have a broad meaning
Allah spoke to me during Miraj
exp: The hadith of the six distinctions (Muslim) lists: concise comprehensive speech, victory through awe, lawful spoils, the earth as a place of prayer and purification, being sent to all people, and the sealing of prophethood — speaking with Allah is not among them.

q: Deliberately changing the Qur'anic text while reciting is...
a: Forbidden; deliberate distortion of meaning can be kufr
Considered a major sin but does not take one out of Islam
exp: Deliberately altering the text of the Quran is forbidden, and consciously changing Allah's words to distort their meaning is disbelief.

q: What will the first people entering Paradise drink with their food?
exp: In the hadith of Thawban, after their meal the people of Paradise drink from a spring called Salsabil (Muslim; cf. 76:18).

q: Hadith of Muslim: “Let none of you, when dying, expect anything from the Almighty and Great Allah...” - what?
a: In addition to payment for actions
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Let none of you die except thinking well of Allah” (Muslim).

q: According to the hadith: “The debt must be paid first...” What do you mean?
exp: Ali reported that the Prophet ﷺ ruled that a deceased person's debt is paid before executing the bequest (at-Tirmidhi).

q: Hadith from al-Bara (radiyallahu anhu): “Visit the sick and accompany the janazah, for...” - why?
a: The reward for this is two qirat.
For this the reward is like Mount Uhud
It reminds you of the Hereafter
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Visit the sick and follow funerals, for they remind you of the Hereafter” (Ahmad).

q: Hadith of Ibn Majah: He who sympathizes with a Muslim in his misfortune will receive reward on the Day of Resurrection. What exactly?
a: Will hide his sins from people
Will clothe him in garments of honour
exp: In the hadith in Ibn Majah, Allah will clothe the one who consoles his brother in misfortune in garments of honour on the Day of Judgement.

q: Muslim: “Two things are a sign of disbelief: defamation of the origin of others and...”
a: Indifference to the origin of one's lot
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Two things among people are from disbelief: attacking lineage and wailing over the dead” (Muslim).

q: What is the legal status of washing the body of the deceased in Islam?
exp: Washing the deceased is fard kifayah: if some perform it, the obligation is lifted from the rest.

q: Who has the greatest right to wash the dead?
a: The one to whom the deceased bequeathed it
exp: The person the deceased named in his will has the greatest right, as Abu Bakr willed his wife Asma bint Umays to wash him.

q: The Meccans buried their dead with a shakk (a depression at the bottom of the grave), and the Medinans buried their dead with a lahd (a depression towards the grave). How was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ buried?
exp: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was buried in a grave with a side niche (lahd); he said: “The lahd is for us, and the shaqq for others.”

q: Who dug the grave for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?
exp: Abu Talhah al-Ansari used to dig graves with a lahd and dug the Prophet's ﷺ grave.

q: What do those who washed the dead need?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever washes a deceased person, let him take a bath”; most scholars consider this recommended, not obligatory.

q: What is the name of the hadith in the chain of which there is no companion of the Prophet ﷺ?
exp: A mursal hadith is one that a Successor narrates directly from the Prophet ﷺ without naming the Companion.

q: In the hadith: in Medina, when the adhan sounds, the shaitan runs away, emitting gases. Afterwards he returns; during iqamah he runs away again, and then stands between the person and his heart, admonishing him. How far does he run?
a: At a distance of 1.5 days travel
exp: In the hadith in Muslim, Shaytan flees from the adhan as far as ar-Rawha', about 36 miles from Medina — around a day and a half's journey.

q: Which verses did the Prophet ﷺ call “unique and all-encompassing”?
a: “Whoever has done good as an atom of dust...” - Az-Zalzala, 7–8
The last verses of Surah Al-Baqarah
exp: The Prophet ﷺ called verses 99:7–8 unique and all-encompassing: every atom's weight of good and evil will be recompensed.

q: Who is truly strong according to the words of the Prophet ﷺ?
a: The one who wins in battle
The one who controls his anger
Someone who goes to the gym often
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The strong one is not the one who wins in wrestling, but the one who controls himself when angry” (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: Who does the Prophet ﷺ say is a Muslim?
a: Who reads the Koran a lot
The one from whose tongue and hands other Muslims are safe
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “A Muslim is one from whose tongue and hand other Muslims are safe” (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: Who performed Janaza prayer over ‘Umar (radiyallahu anhu)?
exp: Before his death Umar appointed Suhayb ar-Rumi to lead the prayers until the council chose a caliph, and Suhayb led his funeral prayer.

q: What is the reward for the one who performs janaza prayer over a dead person in the mosque?
a: It is forbidden to bring a body into the mosque
exp: Funeral prayer in the mosque is permissible — the Prophet ﷺ prayed over Suhayl ibn Bayda in the mosque (Muslim) — and praying over the deceased earns one qirat of reward.

q: Who should not perform Janazah prayer on?
exp: “Do not ever pray over any of them who has died…” (9:84); funeral prayer is not performed over a disbeliever.

q: Surah Al-Fath (48:20) says: “Allah promised you rich booty that you would capture, and granted it to you in advance...” What are we talking about?
exp: According to most exegetes, the “spoils hastened for you” refer to Khaybar, taken soon after Hudaybiyyah.

q: What tribe of Jews lived in Khaybar?
exp: The Banu Nadir, expelled from Medina and led by Huyayy ibn Akhtab, settled in Khaybar and led its community.

q: What does the verses of Surah Al ‘Imran (131, 133) indicate regarding Heaven and Hell?
a: Heaven and Hell were created before the creation of man
They will be created on the Day of Resurrection
They will be created after the trial is completed
exp: Allah says the Fire “has been prepared for the disbelievers” (3:131) and Paradise “has been prepared for the pious” (3:133); the past tense shows both already exist.

q: Surah An-Najm (53:16) says: “The lotus was covered with that which covered it.” What do you mean?
a: There's an angel on every leaf
Its beauty is indescribable to creatures
exp: Hadiths and exegesis describe golden moths, angels and indescribable beauty covering the Lote Tree — these accounts are compatible.

q: What is the state of the soul of a devout Muslim after death?
a: It enters Paradise only after the Judgement
It dwells in the bliss of Paradise even before the Day of Judgement
It waits for bodily resurrection in the grave
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The soul of the believer is a bird feeding from the trees of Paradise until Allah returns it to its body on the Day of Resurrection” (Malik, Ahmad).

q: How many levels are there in Paradise?
a: As many as there are suras in the Qur'an
The same number of verses in the Qur'an
As many as there are juz' in the Qur'an
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “In Paradise there are a hundred levels Allah has prepared for those who strive in His cause; between each two levels is like between heaven and earth” (al-Bukhari).

q: If you ask Allah for Paradise, which level should you ask for (according to the hadith)?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “When you ask Allah, ask for al-Firdaws, for it is the middle and highest part of Paradise” (al-Bukhari).

q: Who is Ridwan?
exp: In the reports, Ridwan is the name given to the angel who guards Paradise.

q: What is the position of Paradise after the Day of Judgment?
a: It will be completely filled with people and genies
There will be a place in it, and Allah will create creatures to fill it.
He will disappear after the trial
He will become part of this land
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said space will remain in Paradise, and Allah will create new beings for it (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: How many gates does Heaven have?
exp: Paradise has eight gates, among them ar-Rayyan for those who fast (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: Whose ummah will be the second largest in Paradise?
exp: In the hadith of the nations shown to the Prophet ﷺ, after his own ummah he saw a huge multitude — the people of Musa (peace be upon him) (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: “Indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of those which you count.” In which surah is this verse?
exp: This is verse 22:47 of Surah Al-Hajj; a day of a thousand years is also mentioned in 32:5, and a day of fifty thousand years in 70:4.

q: What is the name of the place where the deeds of the inhabitants of Paradise are recorded?
exp: “The record of the righteous is in ‘Illiyyun” (83:18); the record of the wicked is in Sijjin (83:7).

q: How will the inhabitants of Paradise sit at the Throne of Allah on Fridays?
a: By how much they read the Koran
According to who was the first to come to Juma prayer
Based on how long the tahajjud was performed
exp: Reports about the “Day of Increase” say that people in Paradise will be near to Allah according to how early they came to Friday prayer.

q: The hadith says that Heaven and Hell had an argument. Allah has decreed: “Paradise is you...”. What's next?
exp: Allah said to Paradise: “You are My mercy, through which I show mercy to whom I will”, and to Hell: “You are My punishment” (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: What will be the possession of the last one to enter Paradise?
exp: Allah will tell the last person to enter Paradise: “You have the like of the world and ten times more” (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: Who will be the first to open the gates of Heaven?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “I will come to the gate of Paradise and ask for it to be opened. The keeper will ask: ‘Who are you?’ I will say: ‘Muhammad.’ He will say: ‘I was ordered not to open for anyone before you’” (Muslim).

q: What is the highest pleasure in Paradise?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said the people of Paradise will be given nothing more beloved to them than looking at their Lord (Muslim).

q: What is the name of the tree in Paradise under which a rider can ride for a hundred years?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said there is a tree in Paradise in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years; some narrations name it Tuba.

q: Which four rivers are mentioned in the Qur'an as rivers of Paradise? (47:15)
a: Water, wine, olive oil and milk
exp: Paradise has rivers of unspoiled water, milk whose taste never changes, wine delicious to drinkers, and purified honey (47:15).

q: How will food be removed from the bodies of the inhabitants of Paradise?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said the people of Paradise do not relieve themselves; their food leaves them as sweat smelling of musk (Muslim).

q: Surah Al-Insan (76:21) speaks of the clothes of the inhabitants of Paradise: “from sundus and istabraq.” What is this?
exp: Sundus is fine silk (satin) and istabraq is thick silk brocade.

q: Surah Yunus (10:26) says: “For those who do good, the best and the best.” What is an "additive"?
a: Opportunity to see the Face of Allah
exp: The Prophet ﷺ explained that the “increase” is seeing the Face of Allah after entering Paradise (Muslim).

q: What, according to the hadith, are the houses in Paradise built of?
a: Plaster of musk, earth of saffron
All of the above are true
exp: The Prophet ﷺ described the dwellings of Paradise: bricks of gold and silver, mortar of musk, pebbles of pearls and rubies, soil of saffron (at-Tirmidhi).

q: What is the distance between the doors of the gates of Paradise, according to the hadith of Muslim?
a: Distance of a hundred years' journey
exp: In the report in Muslim, the distance between the two panels of a gate of Paradise is forty years' journey.

q: The Prophet ﷺ said: “I swear by Him in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad! The inhabitant of Paradise has been granted the power of... men..."
a: The strength of a hundred men
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said a dweller of Paradise will be given the strength of a hundred men (at-Tirmidhi).

q: What is Al-Wasila?
a: One of the degrees of Firdaus
Name of the source in Paradise
exp: Al-Wasilah is the highest station in Paradise, meant for only one of Allah's servants, whom the Prophet ﷺ hoped would be him; it is asked for in the supplication after the adhan (Muslim).

q: How many levels does Hell have?
exp: “It has seven gates, and for every gate is a portion of them” (15:44); scholars derive seven levels of Hell from this.

q: Jahannam, Laza, Khutama, Sa'ir, Sakar, Jahim, Hawiah - what is it?
exp: In the exegetical tradition, these names mentioned in the Quran are assigned to the seven levels of Hell.

q: What is the meaning of the word "Hawiyah"?
exp: “Hawiyah” means abyss: “…his refuge will be an abyss” (101:9).

q: At what level of Hell will there be hypocrites (munafiks)?
exp: “Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire” (4:145).

q: What is the name of the bridge stretched over Hell?
exp: The Sirat is the bridge over Hell that all people will cross, each according to their deeds.

q: What is the fuel of Hell?
exp: “…the Fire whose fuel is people and stones” (2:24, 66:6).

q: What is the name of the tree that grows through the levels of Hell?
exp: “It is a tree that grows from the bottom of Hell” (37:64) — the tree of zaqqum.

q: What are the fruits of Zakkum like?
a: On the heads of the devils
exp: “Its fruit is as if it were the heads of devils” (37:65).

q: What is the name of the guard of Hell?
exp: The people of Hell will call: “O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us” (43:77); Malik is the keeper of Hell.

q: How many angels will hold on to each bridle when Hell is brought on Judgment Day?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Hell will be brought that Day with 70,000 reins, each pulled by 70,000 angels” (Muslim).

q: How many reins will Hell have when it is brought on the Day of Judgment?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Hell will be brought that Day with 70,000 reins, each pulled by 70,000 angels” (Muslim).

q: How many angels guard Hell?
exp: “Over it are nineteen” (74:30): the Quran names nineteen angel guardians of Hell.

q: Who is the inhabitant of Hell?
a: Only Muslims whose sins outweigh their good deeds
exp: Disbelievers and hypocrites will be in Hell forever, and Muslims whose sins outweigh their deeds for a time, unless Allah forgives them.

q: What part of the fire of Hell is the fire that we use on earth?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Your fire is one seventieth part of the fire of Hell” (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: How many years will a stone thrown into Hell fall until it reaches the bottom?
exp: The Companions heard a crash, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “That is a stone thrown into Hell seventy years ago; only now has it reached the bottom” (Muslim).

q: What color is the fire of Hell?
exp: The hadith says the fire of Hell was heated a thousand years until red, a thousand until white and a thousand until black, so it is black and dark (at-Tirmidhi).

q: There will be a neck by the fire that will say: “Three have been entrusted to me...” Who is the third?
exp: A neck will emerge from the Fire and say: “I am entrusted with three: every stubborn tyrant, whoever invokes another god besides Allah, and image-makers” (at-Tirmidhi).

q: The Prophet ﷺ was shown Hell. What tribe was the woman from?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ saw in Hell a woman of Himyar who locked up a cat and did not feed it until it died (Muslim).

q: Whoever cuts down a tree... Allah will throw him head down into the fire.
a: Tree on the territory of the Haram
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever cuts down a lote tree (sidr), Allah will plunge his head into the Fire” (Abu Dawud) — referring to a desert tree giving shade to travellers.

q: How many people out of every thousand will end up in Hell?
exp: On the Day of Judgement Allah will tell Adam to bring out the people of the Fire: 999 of every thousand, most of them from Gog and Magog (al-Bukhari).

q: The distance between the shoulders of a non-believer in Hell will be equal to...
a: Three days' journey for the horseman
One day of the rider's journey
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The distance between the shoulders of a disbeliever in the Fire is three days' journey for a swift rider” (Muslim).

q: In the hadith it says the thickness of the skin of a disbeliever will be...
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The thickness of a disbeliever's skin is forty-two cubits” (at-Tirmidhi).

q: The lightest punishment in Fire...
exp: The lightest punishment will be Abu Talib's: sandals of fire that make his brain boil (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: Verily, the inhabitants of Fire will weep...
exp: The hadith says the people of the Fire will weep until their tears run dry, then weep blood (Ibn Majah).

q: On the Day of Judgment the Sun and Moon will...
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The sun and moon will be folded up on the Day of Resurrection” (al-Bukhari); al-Bazzar's version adds “…in the Fire”.

q: What are the two conditions for deeds to be accepted in Islam?
a: Sincerity for Allah and conformity to the Sunnah
Intention alone without following the Sunnah
exp: A deed is accepted if done sincerely for Allah and in accordance with the Prophet's ﷺ Sunnah: “Whoever does a deed not in accordance with our matter, it will be rejected” (Muslim).

q: What is *harj*?
exp: The Companions asked: “What is harj?” The Prophet ﷺ answered: “Killing”, naming its increase a sign of the Hour (al-Bukhari).

q: From the hadith: “The Hour will not come until the land of the Arabs once again…”
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The Hour will not come until the land of the Arabs returns to meadows and rivers” (Muslim).

q: The time will come only when...
a: The worst people will remain on earth
The ground will collapse in Sham
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The Hour will only come upon the worst of people” (Muslim).

q: "I was sent..." (hadith about the nearness of the Hour). What is correct?
exp: The meaning is that the Prophet ﷺ was sent right before the Hour. In al-Bukhari and Muslim: “I and the Hour have been sent like these two,” and he pointed to his index and middle fingers.

q: Who was called Banu al-Asfar?
exp: Banu al-Asfar (“sons of the yellow one”) is what the Arabs called the Romans (Byzantines).

q: How many liars will appear?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said the Hour will not come until about thirty liars appear, each claiming to be a prophet (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: What does "red treasury" mean?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ was given “the two treasures, the red and the white”, understood as the gold of Byzantium and the silver of Persia (Muslim).

q: What destroys Islam?
a: The hypocrite's arguing with the Quran
exp: Umar said: “Islam is destroyed by the slip of a scholar, the hypocrite's arguing with the Quran, and the rule of misguided leaders” (ad-Darimi).

q: The Prophet ﷺ said: the omen of this Hour will be the disappearance of knowledge, the rooting of ignorance, people will drink a lot of wine, and it will become widespread...
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Among the signs of the Hour are the disappearance of knowledge, the spread of ignorance, drinking wine and adultery” (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: The false prophet Musailima was killed under Abu Bakr (radiyallahu anhu). Who killed him?
exp: Musaylimah was killed by Wahshi — the same man who killed Hamzah at Uhud before accepting Islam — who said he hoped it would atone for his earlier deed.

q: The Hour of Judgment will not come until time is shortened. A year will become like a month, a month like a week, a week like a day, a day like an hour, and an hour like...
a: The time of two rak'ats of the sunnah before Fajr
The disappearance of the evening dawn after the Maghreb
The smoldering time of the firebrand
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said that before the Hour time will contract until an hour is like the burning of a palm frond (at-Tirmidhi).

q: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The Hour of Judgment will not come until those passing by the graves speak...”
a: “May Allah have mercy on him, he does not see what we see”
“It would be better if I were in his place”
“Allah saved them from the trials to which we are subjected”
“As-salamu ‘alaikum, inhabitants of the graves. May Allah have mercy on you and on us who join you."
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The Hour will not come until a man passes by a grave and says: ‘I wish I were in his place’” (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: There is disagreement about the children of polytheists. According to one strong opinion, what will happen to them on the Day of Judgment?
a: They will enter Paradise without testing
They will be servants of the people of Paradise
exp: According to one strong view based on hadiths, the deceased children of polytheists will be tested on the Day of Judgement; another view holds they are in Paradise.

q: As-Sahih 2315. It is narrated from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr (radiyallahu anhu) that the Prophet ﷺ said: “The one who is entrusted with property for safekeeping is not responsible for it if...”
a: It is cheaper than one dinar
It's been there for over a year
Something happened to him through no fault of his own.
The owner of the property died
exp: A trustee is not liable for property entrusted to him if it is lost through no fault or negligence of his own.

q: Sahih 2639. From ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr (radiyallahu anhu) it is reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “The best type of sadaq is...”
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said the best charity is reconciling between people.

q: Which of the following remembrances is authentically established after the obligatory prayer?
a: "Astaghfirullah" (3 times), then "Allahumma anta as-Salamu wa minka as-Salam..."
A long personal dua with raised hands after every fard
There is no prescribed dhikr after fard
exp: After finishing the prayer the Prophet ﷺ sought forgiveness three times, then said: “Allahumma anta as-Salam wa minka as-salam, tabarakta ya dhal-jalali wal-ikram” (Muslim).

q: Which dhikr did the Prophet ﷺ especially recommend after the obligatory prayer?
a: Raise of hands and long sincere dua
Tasbih, tahmid and takbir 33 times each
exp: After prayer the Prophet ﷺ taught saying “SubhanAllah”, “Alhamdulillah” and “Allahu akbar” 33 times each, saying no one would surpass its reward except those who do the same (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: Wiping your face with your hands after completing dua - is this sunnah?
exp: Most hadith experts consider the reports about wiping the face after supplication weak, so many scholars do not count it as Sunnah.

q: A sick man was in a very serious condition. The Prophet ﷺ asked: “What is the matter with you?” He replied: “I asked Allah to punish me in this world.” The Prophet ﷺ taught him a supplication from verse 2:201. Which one?
a: “O Allah! You are the healer - heal me, truly there is no healing except Yours."
“La ilakha illya Anta, subhanaka, inni kuntu minaz-zalimin”
“Allahumma, Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasana wa fil-ahirati hasana wa kina ‘azaba-n-Nar”
“The hearts of believers are comforted and healed by the remembrance of Allah”
exp: The Prophet ﷺ told the sick man: “Why did you not say: ‘Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter and protect us from the punishment of the Fire’?” (Muslim).

q: What should you say to the person who said to you: “May Allah forgive you!” (Gafar-Allah laka!)
a: Wa laka! (and may Allah forgive you too)
exp: The reply to “Ghafara Allahu laka” is “Wa laka” — “and you too”.

q: The Prophet ﷺ said: “O people! Repent to Allah, verily I bring repentance to Him... once a day.”
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “O people, repent to Allah, for I repent to Him a hundred times a day” (Muslim).

q:
The Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever says ten times:
“La ilaha illa-Llahu wahdahu la sharika lahu, la-hul-mulku wa la-hul-hamdu wa huwa ‘ala kulli shai’in kadir”
- he’s like...”
a: One who freed three slaves from the descendants of Isma'il
One who freed four slaves from the descendants of Isma'il
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said whoever says it ten times is like one who freed four slaves from the descendants of Isma'il (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: What is the sunnah ruling for someone who performs night prayer with wudu made in the evening?
a: It is permissible and recommended to keep one's wudu
It is permissible only when ill
exp: Wudu remains valid until something breaks it, so one may pray at night with the wudu made in the evening; sleeping in a state of wudu is praiseworthy.

q: What did the words of the prophet Ibrahim (alaihis salam) say to Ismail’s wife mean: “Tell him to strengthen the threshold of his door”?
a: The door is shaky because of the threshold
Let him strengthen his marriage with his wife
Let him repair the door of his house
exp: To Isma'il's first wife Ibrahim sent the message “change the threshold” (divorce), and to the second, grateful one, “keep the threshold firm”, i.e. keep this marriage (al-Bukhari).

q: Surah Al-Hujurat (49), verse 12: “...And do not seek out...”. What are we talking about?
a: Don't spy on others, looking for their flaws.
exp: “…and do not spy (la tajassasu)” (49:12) forbids searching out other people's faults and secrets.

q: Surah Yusuf, verse 87: “Indeed, no one loses hope in the mercy of Allah except the disbelievers.” Is it losing hope?
exp: Despairing of Allah's mercy is counted among the major sins: “No one despairs of Allah's mercy except the disbelievers” (12:87).

q: In Medina there lived a man named Abu Juhaina. He had two measuring cups: with one he measured, and with the other he asked to measure for him. On his occasion, verses 1–3 of Surah “The Weighers” (Al-Mutaffifin) were revealed. What is this sin?
exp: Cheating in measure is a major sin: “Woe to those who give short measure, who take full measure from others but give less when measuring for them” (83:1–3).

q: A long hadith states that the Prophet ﷺ said: “O ‘Abbas! Oh uncle! Should I give you a gift? -What gift are we talking about?
a: Taught him how to make dua Qunut
Freed him from captivity after Badr
exp: The Prophet ﷺ taught his uncle al-Abbas Salat at-Tasbih, in which “SubhanAllah, walhamdulillah, wa la ilaha illallah, wallahu akbar” is repeated 300 times over four rak'ahs (Abu Dawud).

q: According to hadiths, is it forbidden to withhold surplus water (when others need it)?
a: It is disliked but not forbidden
Only if the water was purchased
exp: The Prophet ﷺ forbade withholding surplus water so as not to prevent grazing (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: The hadith about the hypocrite states three qualities, but there is a hadith with a fourth. Call this additional quality.
a: When he argues, he behaves outrageously
Dayus (he doesn't care what the family does)
exp: The version listing four traits of a hypocrite adds: “…and when he argues, he behaves outrageously” (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q:
Musnad Ahmad 3138. Abu Huraira reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Whoever listens carefully to one verse of the Qur'an is written down... which will be multiplied.
And for the one who reads aloud, it will become a light for him on the Day of Judgment.”
exp: In the hadith in Ahmad, one who listens to a verse earns a multiplied good deed, and one who recites it will have light on the Day of Judgement.

q:
Silsila al-Sahiha 549. Musnad Ahmad 6/21.
Fadala ibn Ubayd narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said during the farewell Hajj:
"Mu'min is the one..."
a: Who is zealous in worshiping Allah
Who fulfills all five pillars of Islam
Who recognizes the six pillars of Iman
The one whom people trust with their property and lives
exp: In the hadith of Fadalah ibn Ubayd: “The believer is one whom people trust with their property and lives” (Ahmad).

q:
From the hadith of Fadal ibn Ubaid that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Muslim is the one..."
a: Who recites the five obligatory prayers?
Who was born into a Muslim family
Who does not harm people with his tongue or hands
exp: In the same hadith: “The Muslim is one from whose tongue and hand people are safe.”

q:
From the hadith of Fadal ibn Ubaid that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Mujahid is the one..."
a: Who fights in the path of Allah
Who fights with his soul to submit to Allah
Who defends his life, honor and property
Who submitted to the Muslim ruler
exp: In the same hadith: “The mujahid is one who strives against his own soul in obedience to Allah.”

q:
From the hadith of Fadal ibn Ubaid that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“And the muhajir is the one...”
a: Who migrated in the path of Allah
exp: In the same hadith: “The muhajir is one who abandons sins and wrongdoing.”

q:
Sahih al-Jami' al-Saghir 868.
According to Anas ibn Malik, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“The most merciful in my ummah is...”
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The most merciful of my ummah to my ummah is Abu Bakr, the firmest in Allah's matters is Umar, the most modest is Uthman…” (at-Tirmidhi).

q:
According to Anas ibn Malik, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“The best judge in my ummah is...”
exp: In the same hadith, Ali ibn Abi Talib is named the best judge (Ibn Majah).

q:
According to Anas ibn Malik, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“He knows best what is forbidden and what is permitted...”
exp: In the same hadith: “…the one who knows best the lawful and unlawful is Mu'adh ibn Jabal.”

q:
According to Anas ibn Malik, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“He knows inheritance issues best of all...”
exp: In the same hadith: “…the one who knows best the laws of inheritance is Zayd ibn Thabit.”

q:
According to Anas ibn Malik, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best reciter of the Qur'an is..."
exp: In the same hadith: “…the best reciter of the Quran is Ubayy ibn Ka'b.”

q:
According to Anas ibn Malik, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Each community had its own confidant, and the confidant of my community is...”
exp: In the same hadith: “…every nation has a trustworthy one, and the trustworthy one of this ummah is Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah.”

q:
As-Silsilya as-Sahiha 2831.
“Indeed, the servant of Allah will be rewarded for everything he spends, except what he spends on...”
exp: The hadith says a person is rewarded for everything he spends except for spending on building beyond need.

q: According to some Companions, what is the reward for four rak'ahs prayed after Isha?
a: Like freeing 10 slaves from the descendants of Isma'il
As if he was fasting on the day of 'Arafat
As if he was praying on the night of Laylat al-Qadr
exp: It is reported from some Companions that four rak'ahs after Isha are like the same prayer on Laylat al-Qadr in reward.

q: At the beginning of the prophecy, the Battle of Bu'as took place in Yathrib between two tribes. Between whom?
exp: The Battle of Bu'ath between the related tribes of Aws and Khazraj took place about five years before the Hijra and weakened both.

q: 12 years after the beginning of the prophecy, 12 people from Yathrib (10 from Khazraj and 2 from Aus) met with Muhammad ﷺ, who accepted Islam and took an oath. Why is this called the first oath of Aqaba?
a: Aqaba is a valley near Mecca
This was the name of the well near the road from Medina to Mecca
This is a large tamarisk tree, which was given the name Aqaba
This is the name of the hill
exp: Al-Aqabah is a mountain pass near Mina where the people of Medina secretly met the Prophet ﷺ and gave their pledge.

q: How many times did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform Hajj after the Hijra?
exp: After the Hijra the Prophet ﷺ performed Hajj once — the Farewell Hajj in 10 AH — and Umrah four times.

q: At the time of accepting Islam, what religion did Salman al-Farisi adhere to?
exp: Salman al-Farisi was born into a Zoroastrian family, later became a Christian and searched for the true faith until he met the Prophet ﷺ in Medina.

q: Surah An-Nur, verses 11-21, were revealed about this woman. Who is she?
exp: Verses 24:11–21 were revealed about the slander against Aishah (the incident of al-Ifk), affirming her innocence.

q: In the 5th year of the Hijri, she participated with the Prophet ﷺ in the battle of Banu Mustaliq, known as the Mureisi Campaign. Who is she?
exp: Aishah accompanied the Prophet ﷺ on the expedition to Banu al-Mustaliq, and on the way back the incident that led to the slander occurred.

q: Is this al-hukm?
exp: Hukm is the legal ruling in Sharia: obligatory, recommended, permissible, disliked or forbidden.

q: What is considered the best time for the morning adhkar?
a: From the start of Fajr until dawn
From Fajr until the sun's zenith
exp: The best time for the morning adhkar is from dawn (Fajr) until sunrise; some scholars extend it until midday.

q: What is considered the best time for the evening adhkar?
exp: The best time for the evening adhkar is after Asr until sunset; some scholars extend it into the early night.

q: In the khutbah it is said: "The worst matters are ...". What is meant?
exp: In his sermons the Prophet ﷺ said: “The worst of matters are newly invented ones, and every innovation is misguidance” (Muslim).

q: From the hadith: prayer in the Quba mosque is like...?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Prayer in the mosque of Quba' is like an Umrah” (at-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah).

q: Where was Masjid ad-Dirar (Mosque of Unbelief) built?
a: In the territory of Banu Qaynuqa
exp: Masjid ad-Dirar was built by hypocrites in Quba', near the Quba' mosque, to sow division; Allah forbade the Prophet ﷺ from praying in it (9:107–108).

q: What objects are allowed by Sharia law to kiss?
a: Place of prayer of Ibrahim (maqam of Ibrahim)
Tomb of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
All of the above can be kissed
exp: The Prophet ﷺ kissed the Black Stone, and Umar said: “Had I not seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kiss you, I would not have kissed you”; kissing other objects is not prescribed.

q: In the pre-Islamic era, the Aus and Khazraj tribes performed Hajj to this idol. Which one?
exp: Aishah reported that before Islam the Aws and Khazraj entered ihram for Manat, which stood at al-Mushallal (al-Bukhari).

q: Are the terms "tawhid" and "shahada" synonyms?
exp: Tawhid is the belief in Allah's oneness; the shahadah is the testimony “There is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah”, which expresses tawhid and affirms the Prophet's message.

q: Which surah has the second most verses after Al-Baqarah?
exp: Surah Ash-Shu'ara has 227 verses — more than any surah except Al-Baqarah (286); Ali 'Imran has 200. By length of text An-Nisa is usually counted second, but it has fewer verses — 176.

q: Is it permissible for the imam in the mosque to combine and shorten prayers if it is raining outside?
exp: Most scholars allow combining prayers in the mosque in rain but not shortening them, since shortening is only for travel; the Hanafis do not allow combining for rain.

q: Is it permissible to give zakat under the category of fi ar-riqab (freeing slaves/mukatab)?
exp: “Fir-riqab” is one of the eight categories of zakat recipients (9:60): freeing slaves and helping slaves buying their freedom (mukatab).

q: Is it permissible for freedmen of the family of Muhammad ﷺ to receive zakat?
a: He has the right to zakat
He has no right to zakat
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Sadaqah is not lawful for us, and the freed slave of a people is one of them” (Abu Dawud), so the freed slaves of his family also cannot receive zakat.

q: Who is a miskin in Sharia?
a: A person who has some means but not enough for basic needs
A person with no property or income at all
A person with enough for a year
exp: According to the Shafi'is and Hanbalis, a miskin has some means but not enough for basic needs; the Hanafis, conversely, consider the miskin poorer than the faqir.

q: In which surah is the splitting of the moon mentioned?
exp: “The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split” (54:1) — the opening of Surah Al-Qamar (“The Moon”).

q: What is the name of the madhhab, which was written down and systematized by the disciples of the imam - Abu Yusuf and Muhammad?
exp: Abu Hanifah's school was recorded and systematised by his students Abu Yusuf and Muhammad ash-Shaybani.

q: One Jew said to the Prophet ﷺ: “Are you making shirk by saying: “Allah and you have said,” and also...?”
a: Guess by the flight of birds
exp: After the Jew's remark, the Prophet ﷺ instructed swearing by “the Lord of the Ka'bah” and saying “What Allah wills, then what you will” (an-Nasa'i).

q: Who is a faqir (poor person) in Sharia?
a: A person who does not have enough for basic needs
A person with half the required means
A person with a year's food supply
