A person with wealth above nisab
exp: A faqir is one who lacks the means for basic needs or has only a small part of them; according to the Shafi'is and Hanbalis he is poorer than the miskin.

q: “No one was endowed with a better gift than...” (Muslim 1053). What do you mean?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “No one has been given a gift better and more comprehensive than patience” (Muslim).

q: From the hadith: one man confessed his love to the Prophet ﷺ for the sake of Allah. What did the Prophet ﷺ answer him?
a: Get ready for the good news
You will be next to me in Paradise
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “If you love me, prepare for poverty, for poverty comes to one who loves me faster than a flood to its end” (at-Tirmidhi).

q: At one of the following events, Iblis groaned. Under what?
a: When Musa and his people crossed the sea
When Ibrahim threw a stone at him when they met in Mecca
When Nuh (peace be upon him) built the Ark
exp: A report says Iblis groaned four times: when he was cursed, when he was cast down, when Muhammad ﷺ was sent, and when Al-Fatihah was revealed.

q: Sura 2 “Al-Baqarah”, verse 102. In what area did the two angels Harut and Marut teach people witchcraft?
a: In Mesopotamia, in the city of Ur
exp: “…and what was sent down to the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut” (2:102).

q: Surah An-Nisa (Women), verse 51: “...They believe in jibt and taghut...”. What is Jibt according to Hassan al-Basri?
exp: Al-Hasan al-Basri said jibt is “the whisper (voice) of Shaytan”; other exegetes understood it as sorcery or idols.

q: Which two angels in Babylon are mentioned in verse 2:102?
exp: “…and what was sent down to the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut” (2:102).

q: The hadiths report a group that survived and stood by the truth until the Day of Judgment. It is reported from Abu Umama that he was asked: “Where will they be, O Messenger of Allah ﷺ?” What did he say?
exp: Asked where this group would be, the Prophet ﷺ answered: “In Bayt al-Maqdis and its surroundings” (Ahmad).

q: A man found a treasure of gold in his garden. Should he pay tax on it?
a: Determines the nisab and pays zakat from it
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “On buried treasure (rikaz) is one fifth” (al-Bukhari, Muslim), paid immediately without nisab or waiting a year.

q: According to Ibn Mas'ud, which verse is the most voluminous in meaning in the Qur'an?
a: Surah An-Nahl 16:90 — “Indeed, Allah commands justice and excellence...”
Surah At-Talaq 65:3 - “Whoever fears Allah, He creates a way out...”
Surah Az-Zumar 39:53 - “Do not despair of Allah’s mercy”
exp: Ibn Mas'ud called 16:90 the most comprehensive verse of the Quran: it commands justice, excellence and giving to relatives, and forbids indecency and oppression.

q: One of the women asked ‘Aisha: “Which person has the greatest right over me?” She replied: “Your husband.” Then she asked: “Who has more rights to her husband?” What did 'Aisha answer?
exp: Aishah answered that a man's mother has the greatest right over him (al-Hakim, an-Nasa'i).

q: When was the marriage between the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Sawda bint Zam'a concluded?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ married Sawdah bint Zam'ah in Mecca after Khadijah's death, about three years before the Hijra.

q: In the hadith about the seven major sins, indicate a sin that is not included in this hadith.
exp: The seven destructive sins are shirk, sorcery, murder, usury, consuming an orphan's wealth, fleeing battle and slandering chaste women (al-Bukhari, Muslim); arrogance is not in this list.

q: Name the first sin by which creation disobeyed Allah.
exp: The first act of disobedience was Iblis refusing to prostrate to Adam out of arrogance: “He refused and was arrogant” (2:34).

q: What is the kaffarah for zihar according to the Qur'an (58:3-4)?
a: Free a slave; if unable, fast two months; if unable, feed 60 poor people
Fast for three days or feed 10 poor people
exp: The expiation for zihar: free a slave; if unable, fast two consecutive months; if unable, feed sixty poor people (58:3–4).

q: The hadith says: “Tuba for the one who saw me and believed... and another Tuba for the one who...?”
a: Who spends their nights in worship
Who believed in me without seeing me
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Tuba to whoever saw me and believed, and Tuba seven times to whoever believed in me without seeing me” (Ahmad).

q: Tuba is a tree in Paradise: its flowers are covers, its leaves are aba. What are its branches made of?
exp: Reports about the Tuba tree say the garments of the people of Paradise come from its calyces and its branches are of ambergris.

q: In a hadith, the Prophet ﷺ said: “Should I inform you of what is more dangerous and scary for you than al-Masih ad-Dajjal?” What is this?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ named hidden shirk: a man stands to pray and beautifies his prayer because he sees someone watching him (Ibn Majah).

q: What is the zakat on crops irrigated with labour (artificial watering)?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: for crops watered by rain or springs, one tenth; for crops irrigated with labour, half of a tenth (al-Bukhari).

q: The imam goes into bowing while the person behind him is still standing. What should he do?
a: Follow the imam right away without lagging unnecessarily
Finish the whole surah however long it takes
Skip the bowing and go straight to prostration
Wait for the imam to stand and bow separately
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The imam is appointed to be followed: when he bows, bow” (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: When did Hawsa bint ‘Umar become the wife of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?
a: In the 3rd year of the Hijra
In the 5th year of the Hijri
exp: Hafsah was widowed after her husband's death from wounds at Badr or Uhud, and the Prophet ﷺ married her in 3 AH.

q: Which of these wives did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bury with his own hands?
exp: Zaynab bint Khuzaymah, called “mother of the poor”, died a few months after the marriage during the Prophet's ﷺ lifetime; he prayed over her and buried her at al-Baqi'.

q: How many times is the name of Allah "Al-Ahad" mentioned in the Qur'an?
exp: As a name of Allah, al-Ahad appears once in the Quran: “Say: He is Allah, the One (Ahad)” (112:1).

q: Which of these names of Allah are always mentioned in pairs?
exp: “He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden” (57:3); the names “the First” and “the Last” are only mentioned together.

q: Surah At-Tawbah 9:70. Which prophet was sent to the people of 'Ad?
exp: The Prophet Hud (peace be upon him) was sent to ‘Ad, Salih to Thamud, and Shu'ayb to Madyan.

q: Muslim 2642: “This is speedy good news for the believer.” What did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mean?
a: A good deed for which people praise him
exp: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about a man praised for his good deeds and said: “That is the believer's glad tidings given in advance” (Muslim).

q: According to Ibn Mas'ud: patience is half of faith, and complete faith is...?
exp: Ibn Mas'ud said: “Patience is half of faith, and certainty (yaqin) is the whole of faith” (al-Bukhari, mu'allaq).

q: ‘Aria is a thing taken for temporary use in fiqh. What did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ take from Safwan ibn Umayya on the day of the Battle of Hunayn?
exp: Before Hunayn the Prophet ﷺ borrowed coats of mail from Safwan ibn Umayyah, not yet a Muslim, as a guaranteed loan (Abu Dawud).

q: Sulh in Arabic is reconciliation...?
a: In a property dispute between two parties
exp: Sulh means reconciliation in general — between spouses, warring parties and in property disputes.

q: How many main types of naskh (abrogation) are identified in 'ulum al-Qur'an?
exp: The Quranic sciences distinguish three kinds of abrogation: both text and ruling abrogated; text abrogated but ruling kept; ruling abrogated but text kept.

q: How did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ know the end of a particular surah?
a: By the revelation of the basmallah
exp: Ibn Abbas said: “The Prophet ﷺ did not know where a surah ended until ‘Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim’ was revealed to him” (Abu Dawud).

q: Which of the companions had the suras in the order in which we read the Koran today?
exp: The order of surahs in today's Mushaf is the one fixed in the copies sent out by the caliph Uthman; the personal codices of Ali and Ubayy had different orders.

q: Which of the following titles is the book of Allah?
a: All of the above means the book of Allah
exp: All these names occur in the Quran for the Scripture: Quran (recitation), Furqan (criterion), Kitab (book), Dhikr (reminder) and Tanzil (revelation).

q: During mi'raj, in which sky did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ meet the prophets 'Isa and Yahya (peace be upon them)?
exp: During the Ascension the Prophet ﷺ met Adam in the first heaven and Isa and Yahya in the second (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: Sura 17 “Al-Isra”, verse 57: “Those to whom they call in prayer themselves seek closeness to their Lord...” Who are we talking about?
a: About people who worship the righteous
About those who worship dead ancestors
exp: Ibn Mas'ud explained: people worshipped jinn who then became Muslim, while their worshippers kept worshipping them (al-Bukhari); other views say it refers to angels, Isa and Uzayr.

q: Which of the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died last?
exp: According to the best-known view, Umm Salamah was the last of the Prophet's ﷺ wives to die, around 61 AH.

q: She married the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the year 7 AH, and the mediator in the marriage was Najashi (the ruler of Ethiopia). Who is she?
exp: Umm Habibah (Ramlah bint Abi Sufyan) lived in Abyssinia; the Negus concluded her marriage to the Prophet ﷺ in absentia and paid her dowry.

q: Before the battle, this prophet looked at the sun and said: “You are forced and I am forced. O Allah, delay it for me a little." Who are we talking about?
exp: The hadith tells of a prophet for whom the sun was held back until he conquered a city; in Ahmad's narration he is named Yusha' ibn Nun.

q: Which group was the first Muslim to break away from Islam?
exp: The first sect to split from the community were the Kharijites, who under the caliph Ali declared him and his supporters disbelievers.

q: The four entered the Kaaba and each of them performed prayer, turning in a different direction. Which one of them chose the correct direction of the qibla?
a: The one who turned towards Jerusalem
The one who turned to the Black Stone
The one who turned to the Yemen wall
They all chose the right direction
exp: Inside the Ka'bah, a worshipper facing any direction faces part of it; the Prophet ﷺ prayed inside the Ka'bah (al-Bukhari).

q: Jamaat prayer. The imam, out of forgetfulness, rises to the fifth rak'ah. The one standing behind knows that this is the fifth rak'ah. What is its effect?
exp: If a follower knows for certain the imam has stood for an extra rak'ah, he does not follow him but sits and waits to finish the prayer with the imam.

q: She was called "the luckiest old woman." She married her daughters to the most eminent men of her time, and one of her daughters married the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and died in the same place where she married him. Who is she?
exp: Hind bint Awf was called “the most honoured mother-in-law on earth”: her daughters married the Prophet ﷺ, Hamzah, Ja'far and Abu Bakr; her daughter Maymunah married the Prophet ﷺ at Sarif and died there.

q: The seller (farmer) takes money from the buyer against the future harvest. What is the position of such a transaction in Shariah?
exp: This is a salam contract (advance payment for future delivery), which the Prophet ﷺ permitted with a known measure, weight and term (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: He was born in 810 and died in 870. Author of the books “Al-Jami‘ al-Sahih”, “At-Tarikh al-Kabir”, “Al-Adab al-Mufrad”. Who is this?
exp: Imam Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari (194–256 AH) compiled the Sahih, the most authentic hadith collection.

q: At-Tirmidhi 3317. According to the hadith, between the seventh heaven and the Throne there is water. What is the distance from its bottom to the surface?
exp: The hadith in at-Tirmidhi mentions a sea above the seventh heaven, the distance between its top and bottom being like that between the heavens, i.e. 500 years' journey.

q: In what year of the Hijri did the plague known as the Amawas plague begin in Sham, under the reign of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab?
exp: The plague of Amwas in al-Sham in 18 AH took many Companions, including Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah and Mu'adh ibn Jabal.

q: Who read the funeral prayer over ‘Ali ibn Abu Talib?
exp: The funeral prayer over Ali ibn Abi Talib was led by his eldest son al-Hasan.

q: According to Ibn ‘Abbas: the interpretation of the Koran is divided into several sections. How many are there?
exp: Ibn Abbas divided tafsir into four kinds: what the Arabs know from their language, what no one is excused for not knowing, what scholars know, and what only Allah knows.

q: What is the zakat on the fruits of plants that were irrigated with rainwater and groundwater?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: for crops watered by rain or springs, one tenth; for crops irrigated with labour, half of a tenth (al-Bukhari).

q: Were hadith written during the life of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?
a: Yes, some companions wrote them with his permission
No, writing hadith was completely forbidden
There is no authentic report of writing hadith
They were written only after the Prophet's death
exp: Abdullah ibn Amr wrote down the Prophet's ﷺ words with his permission: “Write! By Him in whose hand is my soul, nothing but truth comes out of this” (Abu Dawud).

q: At the beginning of Islam, where did the largest number of Qur'anic scholars die?
a: At the well of Bir Ma'un
exp: Many memorisers of the Quran were killed at the Battle of Yamamah against Musaylimah (11–12 AH), which prompted Abu Bakr to compile the Quran.

q: How was the Qur'an sent down to the nearest sky?
a: It was revealed in several parts
He was revealed in parts over a period of 23 years
He was sent down immediately and completely
exp: Ibn Abbas said the Quran was sent down whole to the lowest heaven on the Night of Decree, then revealed to the Prophet ﷺ in parts over 23 years.

q: The science called Islamic exegesis is the science of...?
exp: Islamic exegesis (tafsir) is the science of interpreting and explaining the meanings of the Quran.

q: The Jew Dhu Nuwas in 523 attempted to convert Christians to Judaism by digging a ditch and burning them in a fire. Which sura of the Koran describes this event?
exp: “Cursed were the people of the ditch, of the fire full of fuel…” (85:4–5); historians link this to the killing of the Christians of Najran under Dhu Nuwas.

q: There is a rule in Sharia: “Everything is prohibited in ibadah except what is permitted.” What is the situation in everyday matters?
a: Everything is prohibited except what is permitted.
Everything that is not prohibited is permitted
exp: The default in everyday matters is permissibility — everything is allowed unless evidence forbids it; in worship it is the reverse, evidence is needed to permit.

q: Surah Al-Fil (The Elephant) describes Abraha's campaign from Yemen to Mecca. What religion did he follow?
exp: Abrahah, governor of Yemen for Christian Abyssinia, built a church in San'a and wanted to destroy the Ka'bah so pilgrims would go there instead.

q: Silsilah al-Sahiha 231. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Carrying out one of Allah’s punishments is better than rain falling for ... days on Allah’s earth.” How many days?
exp: The hadith says carrying out one of Allah's prescribed punishments on earth is better for people than forty days of rain (Ibn Majah, an-Nasa'i).

q: If a person commits a crime unintentionally, is the payment of diya also imposed on his next of kin?
exp: The blood money for unintentional killing is paid by the male paternal relatives (‘aqilah), as the Prophet ﷺ ruled (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: According to the Shafi'i madhhab, what is the amount of diya for a Christian or Jew (ahl al-dhimma) killed by accident?
a: One third of a Muslim's diya
No diya is due except for a Muslim
exp: In the Shafi'i school, the diya for a Jew or Christian is one third of a Muslim's; the Malikis and Hanbalis say half, the Hanafis the full amount.

q: Of the wives and concubines of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, how many of them were maidens?
exp: Of the Prophet's ﷺ wives only Aishah was a virgin at marriage; the others were widows or divorcees.

q: The wives of the Prophet ﷺ are the mothers of the faithful. For committing a virtue or a sin, did they receive reward and punishment in the same way as other Muslim women, or did they have a special degree?
a: They received double reward and double punishment
Up to seven hundred times more
There was no difference from other Muslim women
exp: “O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear immorality, her punishment will be doubled… and whoever is obedient to Allah… We will give her reward twice” (33:30–31).

q: Musa (peace be upon him) delivered a sermon that softened hearts. When asked who has the greatest knowledge on earth, he answered: “I.” Allah pointed him to a slave who had great knowledge. Who was it?
exp: Allah directed Musa (peace be upon him) to a servant at the junction of the two seas with greater knowledge — al-Khidr (18:60–82; al-Bukhari).

q: Surah Ya Sin describes the story of three messengers who arrived in the city. Who are they?
a: They were from among the followers of Musa
exp: The Quran does not name these messengers; Qatadah thought they were envoys of Isa, others that they were messengers of Allah, with no authentic specification.

q: From the hadith: “Knowledge is better than worship, but at its core lies...” What does this mean?
exp: The hadith says: “The merit of knowledge is better than the merit of worship, and the foundation of religion is scrupulous piety (wara')” (at-Tabarani, al-Hakim).

q: Ijara is...?
a: Property lease agreement with option to buy
exp: Ijarah is a hire contract: leasing property or paying for labour for a set fee.

q: Mudaraba is...?
a: Agreement on the provision and management of capital
exp: Mudarabah is a partnership in which one provides capital and the other manages it; profit is shared as agreed and capital losses fall on the owner.

q: In Sharia, a person is considered a scientist...?
a: About whom other scholars have testified that he is a scholar, can give fatwas and knowledge is taken from him
Who memorized the Koran and Hadith
If he holds the position of qadi
If he has an Islamic education
exp: A scholar is one whose knowledge and competence to give fatwas other scholars have recognised and from whom knowledge is taken; memorisation or office alone is not enough.

q: Bukhari and Muslim: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Learn the Qur'an from four: Ibn Mas'ud, Ubay ibn Ka'b, Mu'adh ibn Jabal and...” Who's fourth?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Take the Quran from four: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Salim the freedman of Abu Hudhayfah, Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Mu'adh ibn Jabal” (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: Imam Malik said: “I did not give a fatwa until... people from among those with knowledge testified that I was worthy of it.” How many people was it?
exp: Imam Malik said: “I did not give fatwas until seventy scholars testified that I was qualified for it.”

q: The man sneezed and said: “Alhamdulillah rabbil-‘alamin.” Is this expression consistent with the sunnah?
exp: The Sunnah for one who sneezes is to say “Alhamdulillah”, and “Alhamdulillahi rabbil-‘alamin” is also authentically reported (Abu Dawud, at-Tirmidhi).

q: A man went out to visit a sick man in the morning. What is his reward?
a: 70,000 angels will ask for him until the evening
On this day he himself will not get sick
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever visits a sick person in the morning, seventy thousand angels pray for him until evening” (at-Tirmidhi).

q: After the oath of the second ‘Aqaba, when the treaty of the Prophet ﷺ was concluded with the Aus and Khazraj tribes, the shaitan rose to a hill and shouted to warn the Meccans. What was his name?
exp: After the second pledge of Aqabah, a devil shouted from the mountain to warn Quraysh; the Prophet ﷺ called it “Azabb al-Aqabah” (Ahmad).

q: In the 4th year of the Hijra, a Muslim army of about 1,500 people set out on a campaign, and an enemy army of about 2,000 people came out to meet them. What was the name of this trip?
exp: The expedition of “Badr al-Maw'id” (Second Badr) in 4 AH: the Muslims came to the agreed meeting, but Abu Sufyan turned back with his army, so no battle took place.

q: Which two prayers are described as the hardest for hypocrites?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “No prayer is heavier for the hypocrites than Fajr and Isha” (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: What is forbidden for one going to the mosque or waiting for prayer, since he is considered to be in prayer?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ forbade interlacing the fingers for one going to the mosque or waiting for prayer, for he is considered to be in prayer (Abu Dawud, at-Tirmidhi).

q: Which side of the rows (in congregational prayer) receives the blessing of Allah and the angels?
a: Only the spots immediately behind the imam
The reward is the same for everyone
exp: The hadith says: “Allah and His angels send blessings upon the right sides of the rows” (Abu Dawud).

q: The hadith says: “Take care of this Quran, for, by Him in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, it is slipping away faster than...” What is the comparison?
a: How do the firebrands of an extinguished fire burn out?
Faster than a camel escapes from its tether
How does the morning dew disappear?
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Keep revising the Quran, for it escapes faster than a camel from its tether” (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: Complete the hadith: “The deeds of the one who deliberately leaves prayer will become in vain...”
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever abandons the afternoon prayer (Asr), his deeds become void” (al-Bukhari).

q: The hadith says: “I was ordered to bow to the ground, leaning on ... parts of the body,” and the Prophet ﷺ pointed to them, and also forbade picking up clothes and hair. How many parts is this?
exp: Prostration is made on seven parts of the body: the forehead with the nose, both palms, both knees and the toes of both feet (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: A man has a slave. A slave has property: a house, a car and other property. The owner decided to sell the slave. Does all the property of a slave pass to the new owner?
a: Half of the property is transferred
exp: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever sells a slave who has property, the property belongs to the seller unless the buyer stipulates otherwise” (al-Bukhari, Muslim).

q: A person lent an amount exceeding the nisab. The debtor is unable to repay the debt. Who is responsible for paying zakat?
exp: Zakat on an unrecoverable debt is due from neither the lender nor the borrower; if it is repaid, according to several views zakat is paid for one year.

q: How many letters are in the Arabic alphabet?
exp: The Arabic alphabet has 28 letters (29 if hamzah is counted separately).

q: How many basic short vowel sounds (harakat) are there in Arabic?
exp: There are three basic short vowels: fathah (a), kasrah (i) and dammah (u).
